── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Stick to three runs a week and keep the long run easy to build a solid base.
Answers: No, running every day would raise volume too quickly and could risk injury or burnout. Stick to the three planned runs and rest days.
Next week:
Mon: easy, 5 km, heart rate under 150, flat route. Builds aerobic base.
Tue: rest.
Wed: easy, 6 km, mild hills, heart rate under 150. Adds a touch of intensity.
Thu: rest.
Fri: rest.
Sat: long, 8 km, easy pace, heart rate under 150. Extends aerobic endurance.
Sun: rest.
